newsitem.title: UK: IOD says Labour should raise UK rates and taxes.
newsitem.headline: IOD says Labour should raise UK rates and taxes.

text.p: Britain's incoming Labour government should cool the country's booming economy with a mixture of interest rate and tax increases, Ruth Lea, head of the policy unit at the Institute of Directors said on Friday.
Labour has made itself much more business friendly in its modernisation programme and now needs to prove its commitment to keeping inflation in check, she said.

Gordon Brown, who is expected to be appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer later today, needs to use next Wednesday's monetary meeting with the Bank of England Governor to raise Britain's 6.0 percent interest rates by 25 or 50 basis points, Lea said.
"Strategically it would be a good time to raise rates. He needs quite quickly to get credibility and to be seen to be the tough guy he said he's going to be," Lea said.

"We've got two economies at the moment -- the manufacturing sector and the service sector and the service sector is looking very frothy. We're always in favour of pre-emptive strikes against inflation," she said.

Lea argues Labour could announce a fiscal tightening package of between 2.0 and 4.0 billion stg in the budget expected within two months, in addition to the extra funds likely to be raised through windfall taxes on privatised utility firms.
Lea said the chief contenders for raising extra revenue were ending mortage interest tax relief and restricting tax relief on pension contributions to the basic rate.
In an earlier statement, the IOD said it welcomed the new government and looked forward to working with it.
